verses.pali_roman: Khemiyā tusitā yāmā kaṭṭhakā ca yasassino
verses.english: The Khemiyas, Tusitas and Yāmas, and the Kaṭṭhakas of renown,
the Lambitakas and Lāmaseṭṭhas, the Jotināmas and Āsavas.
The Nimmāṇaratis came. Then came the Paranimmitas.
These ten, tenfold hosts, all of varied hues,
possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,
came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.
These sixty orders of devas, all of varied hues,

verses.pali_roman: Nāmanvayena āgañchuṃ ye caññe sadisā saha:
verses.english: came each according to his name, and others like them with them:
'One whose birth is done with, who has no barrenness, who has crossed the flood, without taint,
let us see the nāga who has crossed the flood, like the moon come clear of darkness.'

verses.pali_roman: Subrahmā paramatto ca puttā iddhimato saha,
verses.english: Subrahmā and Paramatta, sons together with the mighty one,

verses.pali_roman: Sanaṅkumāro tisso ca sopāga samitiṃ vanaṃ.
verses.english: Sanaṅkumāra and Tissa — he too came to the wood, to the assembly.
Over a thousand Brahma worlds the Great Brahmā presides.
Reborn there, radiant, of awesome form, he is of renown.
Ten lords came here, each wielding his own mastery,
and in their midst came Hārita, surrounded by his retinue.

verses.pali_roman: Te ca sabbe abhikkante sinde deve sabrahmake,
verses.english: And when all these had come, the devas with Inda and with Brahmā,
Māra's host came on — see the folly of the Dark One.
'Come. Seize them. Bind them. Let them be bound by lust for you.

verses.pali_roman: Samantā parivāretha. Mā vo muñcittha koci naṃ.’
verses.english: Surround them on every side. Let not one of them escape you.'
So there the great commander sent forth his dark army,
striking the ground with his palm, making a terrifying sound,

vocabulary.meaning: these sixty orders of devas — the line that closes the whole roll-call begun on page 319
Sanankumara, the ever-youthful Brahma, named among the Brahma-world visitors
the Dark One, a name for Mara. His army is the kanhasena, the dark host
folly, dullness. 'See the folly of the Dark One' — the narrator's aside as Mara attacks
